stories.title: Top secrets come spilling out
stories.summary:
Top secrets come spilling out.

In 1917, British analysts deciphered a coded message the German foreign minister sent to one of his country's diplomats vowing to begin "unrestricted submarine warfare" and seeking to win over Mexico with a promise to "reconquer the lost territory in Texas, New Mexico and Arizona" if the US entered the world war.

When it became public, the Zimmerman Telegram caused a sensation, helping propel the US into the conflict against Germany.

stories.title: Father and son arrive in Turkey, seven months after leaving Sydney on a Vespa – video
stories.summary:
Father and son arrive in Turkey, seven months after leaving Sydney on a Vespa – video. Mario Gabrieli and his son Leonardo began their journey from Sydney on their 50-year-old Vespa in early January under a project they named 'I Due Caschi,' meaning 'The Two Helmets' in Italian.

They have now reached the city of Amasya in Turkey.

They expected to continue across Turkey through Cappadocia and Antalya before eventually reaching Trieste in northern Italy, completing a route of nearly 40,000 km. Gabrieli, who was born in Trieste and has lived in Australia for more than two decades,.

stories.title: CBCP stands firm against mining, aggressive development
stories.summary:
CBCP stands firm against mining, aggressive development.

PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – The Catholic Bishops’ Conference of the Philippines (CBCP) has reaffirmed its unwavering opposition to mining and aggressive development, announcing plans to establish a commission dedicated to ecology as part of its intensified advocacy for environmental preservation.

Kidapawan Bishop Jose Colin Bagaforo pointed out the church’s long-standing resistance to destructive projects.

Executive Order No. 121, signed on July.

stories.title: Marcos inspects rehabilitated fish port in Pangasinan
stories.summary:
Marcos inspects rehabilitated fish port in Pangasinan. SUAL, Pangasinan – President Marcos inspected on Thursday the P600-million newly rehabilitated and improved Sual fish port of the Philippine Fisheries Development Authority.

Marcos likewise spoke with officers and crew of Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessels that are patrolling the West Philippine Sea, two of which were recently water-cannoned by the China Coast Guard.
